title: Is using Gen AI as placeholders in games cool and fine?
author: Some__Person1234
selftext: I'm not a developer in any project, but I've been seeing a lot of game companies use ai in their workflow, specifically gen ai. So my concern is that if its fine to use Gen AI as placeholder bg's despite it's infamous impact toward the environment and it's ethics? if not or if you disagree is it fine to still play the game yet pointing out it's usage of it?

comments.author: Binoui
comments.body:
The mainstream public is very against AI, but in the working industry we're way past that point. As a software dev in a big company, 90% of the code I produce is made by AI. And it's well made. I have no idea about the animations/designer side but I'd be surprised to learn it's any different.

There are a lot of valid criticisms about AI use right now. But big companies are always looking to be faster and better, and the environment/ethical debates has never been deciding factors for them.

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
>The mainstream public is very against AI,

Even this isn't true.  The "mainstream public" does not give a shit, from a product perspective they aren't reading the disclaimers and going online to bitch about AI, they're gladly telling ChatGPT their life story and if a video game looks cool and is fun to play - they buy it and play it.  Poll 20 people on the street to ask if they've used AI in the last week and at least 18 are gonna say yes and not be Big Mad about it.

It's only *reddit* that is vehemently anti-AI.  This is very much a topic that falls under "reddit is not representative of reality."

replies.author: EnumeratedArray
replies.body:
I think it's a bit more nuanced than this.

You're right that people don't care if a game looks great and is fun to play, however if a game has the distinctive AI look to it, many will be put off because there's just so much trash out there built in 30mins to make some quick money, that most just won't give a game that has that AI look their time.

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body: I wouldn't really consider that nuanced though - if it has that distinctive "AI slop" look then it by definition does not "look great," which causes the reactions you describe in some people.  But there's plenty of reasons a game might fail the "looks great" check that aren't intrinsically AI related - could just be *old* for example.  You can point to tons of stuff from the PSX era that simply does not hold up to modern graphical fidelity, plenty of players bounce off of it because it does not look aesthetically pleasing when compared to games released in 2026.

replies.author: Binoui
replies.body: I mostly agree with what you're saying, but I think there's still an idea floating (even outside reddit) that IA is slop and low quality work, when in fact it's capable of production grade things. Like any tool, it's how you use it.

replies.author: Bastion80
replies.body: Yeah anti AI is mostly a reddit thing and not worth discussing. I had many discussions already with other developers: at the end their "proof of concept unfinished demos" that have zero purpose ate the most valuable thing on earth, your complete finished and released product that is selling making actual money is "shit" or Ai slop. Yeah buddy... 😂

comments.author: mbcoalson
comments.body: Someone really needs to define how AI was used in a workflow. Was it used to create fake images of what the game world looks like? Lame, the studio deserves to be ridiculed. Are they using AI to iterate through story lines or create more dialogue options? Possibly awesome, we'll have to see. Hating AI to hate AI is such a lazy pop-culture meme assumed as opinion.

comments.author: Still_Ad9431
comments.body: It's fine as placeholder, not final product. Using AI is like using calculator

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
>Using AI is like using calculator

This is an apt analogy, which begs the question, why do you feel that it's only fine as a placeholder and not a final product?

To keep the calculator analogy, we learn how to do long-form algebra and calculus by hand in school so we understand the *theory* behind it, but everyone in the real world making a "final product" (scientists, mathematicians, architects, carpenters, designers, etc.) is straight up using that calculator to create the "final product" because it's faster, easier, and more accurate than doing it by hand.  If AI is aptly equivalent to using a calculator vs longhand math, why is that not an appropriate use?

comments.author: teamharder
comments.body: The cheeseburger the artist would buy with the proceeds would have a far greater environmental impact then me prompting Ludo. I'm not worried about it in the least bit.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
I'm tired of the environment arguments. The amount of "resources" it takes to generate a placeholder asset is 1000x less than the resources spent to have a human model an equivalent placeholder. The one exception is if you can find an asset pack that has what you need, since at that point we're talking exclusively about the bandwidth required to download the pack. Regardless, I can generate assets of placeholder quality on my home PC in about half a second of processing, on a computer whose graphics card is underclocked, and it doesn't push me half as hard as even 10 year old games. It's a fucking stupid argument. I get why people are against Big AI (I am as well) but that's not a technology issue, it's a capitalism issue. And in terms of copyrights, yes it would've been nice if everything had been open source, but actually avoiding training on copyrighted materials was not an option in terms of global competition (but it should've absolutely been open source --- as should all derivatives have been --- to prevent companies from profiteering off of the work of others rather,) but that ship has sailed.

The major industry players have been on board with this for a while. And frankly most of the world is outside of the reddit/influencer bubble. We don't want datacenters by our homes or water sources, just like we don't want giant ass factories near them. But that doesn't mean I won't buy anything that's come out of a factory, either.

I think it's perfectly fine if someone doesn't want to play a game because they don't agree with its usage of AI. The only thing I vehemently disagree with is the rampant brigading that occurs around the issue. It's toxic as hell and built on the back of baseless claims, elitism and gatekeeping. It's unhealthy. If someone wants to eat meat, I can't stop them, and I won't brigade them for their decision. Doesn't mean I'm going to join them, though. Likewise if someone wants to use AI so they can make a game even if there are things they can't do (for instance I make all my own art, animations, and do a lot of the coding, and while I have an ear for music and write my own lyrics I CANNOT play worth a damn, so I use AI for that, code assistance, concept art, market research, content expansion ---such as where I make ten items and provide concrete rules and examples, then have AI expand out using the same formula and create 100 more that I can rapidly look through and assess for changes or implement as is--- etc.) then good for them. Saw a post a while back of a paraplegic talking about how AI has changed their life by allowing them to create things they could only have dreamt of before. Half the responses were berating the person for using AI and that they should've just accepted that they couldn't do art. Fucking egregious.

Oh funny statistic --- a single post on reddit takes more environmental resources than a locally generated image, so don't let people use that argument against you. And don't get me started on the resources consumed by the minute when playing modern games. The only good faith arguments I've heard revolve around IPs, but as noted before --- ship has sailed on that, pandora's box has opened, and the courts have spoken, for better or worse.

replies.author: Binoui
replies.body: You are VASTLY underestimating environnmental aspects. In IA, the issue is not the processing power at the time of the prompt, it's the enormous architecture that was needed to create the model. We're building mega data centers that contains tons of RAM and use tons of energy just to train those models. Also, you're missing the point saying "1 guy making an asset has the same impact as an AI making an asset". The real point of AI is that you're never just making 1 asset per day. Because AI is more efficient, you end up using it a LOT more than a manual user would so the 1-to-1 comparaison is not relevant.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body: So you think that there isn't an extreme development cost for new GPUs? New CPU architecture? What about the development cost of games or the cost of raising a human being up to an age where they can manually create art? If we start talking about the cost to raise these examples to a point where they are producing the final content, the relative burden remains the same. You can't try to include the development cost for one technology, but not for others and call it a fair comparison.

replies.author: Binoui
replies.body: Because AI training is on a whole different scale than everything you've talked about. Entire cities have power grid issues because of data centers. AI is developing faster and bigger than anything we've ever seen, its use is certain to multiply in a few years and who knows what it'll need next. I'm a technology nerd, I love it. But pretending there isn't any cause for concern is straight up reality denial.

replies.author: CycleMother2006
replies.body:
Nvidia spends nearly 100 BILLION a year on R & D for its GPUs. Anthropic spent 7 Billion in 2025 for model training and inference.

So you're right, it's a completely different scale ---> GPU development is over 10x more demanding.

replies.author: Binoui
replies.body: Yeah and guess who those GPU are for ? Idk man you're just being contrarian. You can be pro-AI and still acknowledge the issues like environmental aspects, slop proliferation, concentration of power into the few giants capable of running such a thing.

comments.author: Livid_Standard_3790
comments.body: I think if used correctly it's fine, but my experience is people love to hate on it if they know it's ai

comments.author: Bastion80
comments.body: As a solo developer, I use AI every time I can. I've already shipped and sold software that was 100% coded by AI. My users know it, and nobody complains about it. Just ignore AI haters; they are just a minority that makes a lot of noise. Most people against AI are simply unhappy about others creating and delivering something functional while they have a lot of ideas and will most likely never deliver anything. 99% of non-AI solo developers will never complete their projects and will fail simply because they are against AI (or they use it in secret). In the end, being against new technology is just dumb in general. Smart people embrace new technology and make good use of it.

comments.author: Other-Football72
comments.body: The zealots will not tolerate any use of AI, placeholder or otherwise.
